remarks: Bell only, with tubing added to make it into a trumpet.²  Museum data: "The present slide is a modern replacement made by Peter Barton of Hildenborough in Kent. The original slide was lost before the instrument was acquired by Adam Carse" (info in museum) Tubular slide stays, flat bell stay; ring in slide bow, bell bow; bell docration like 1701 Vermillion**: shells at top of garland; crook inserted between bell and slide sec..SC, are these extra remarks for this trombone or another? Tubular slide says, rather plain. Ferrules have ring pattern. Slide bow has simple ring and plain saddle. Ferrules in slide sec. have ring pattern and match those in bell sec. Bell bow has ring, saddle has zigzag pattern. Flat bell stay has eyelet, hinge, no pin; floral-leaf pattern on on both surfaces, with sleeve on neck-pipe side exactly like #1663, but round rather than octagonal. Bell has considerable terminal flare, like most Kodisch trombones; Nuremberg-style rim wire; shell pattern at top of garland. Inside of bell badly creased & dented. ****In notebook, there are Arnold Myers’ measurements for bell diam. at various axial points. Photo in Horniman files shows how instrument came to museum, configured as a trumpet; this probably explains extra crooks. Examined by the author, August 2003.
